x: At the September Committee meeting the following were admitted to the Club R. Brown, A.

Joe King retired at this point, and Rickards, whose efforts over the Crawley—Bolney section now appeared to be taking their toll, eventually retired a few miles along the road. This necessitated going back to A.

Not that I was alone in my treachery, for there were no less than six other Belgravians in the enemy camp for the day, namely, Freds Rickards and Bentley, R. Martin, Willis, Boddington (a newcomer) and Centurion A.
We now had a 4 points lead and, barring accidents, the Shield looked as good as won. For the final event, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, A.

Thus with one event to go we led the holders by two points, which meant that we had to win the 1 Mile Medley Relay, otherwise a win for Thames Valley would mean us sharing the trophy. In a very fine race A.
In the 440 yards match we had Eddie Pack and he duly won from A.
The time was slow, due mainly to the rough track, but conditions were the same for everybody and our man is to be congratulated on his good running. In the 880 yards Alby Bird met his "bogey man," A.

Robertson, the English International, chased Tom home, but he lost ground each lap at the water jump, which was a very stiff one. In the 880 yards Alby Bird easily qualified for the final, with MacCabe of the L.A.C., as also did A.

The holders of the trophy were the Thames Valley Harriers and after making a very bad start in the 100 yards scratch race, they more or less gave up heart and did not compete in the final event. They took this stand on the condition of the track, and A.

It was one of Pack’s best runs to date and if he could only find something of a finish, I would back him against the best in the country. In the 880 yards Alby Bird ran his usual consistent race and although coming up against his “bogey” man, A.
